title: Digital Wallet & P2P Transfers
summary: A digital wallet like Venmo or PayPal makes sending money between people feel instant, even though moving money between banks takes days. The trick is that both users' balances live in the company's own ledger, so a person-to-person transfer is just an atomic database entry. The slow, risky parts, such as verifying identity, catching fraud, and moving cash in and out of real bank accounts, happen around that core.

walkthrough.title: Send money
walkthrough.text: Ana taps 'Send $20 to Sam' with a note. The app sends the request with an idempotency key so a retry cannot send twice.

walkthrough.title: Check identity, limits, and risk
walkthrough.text: The wallet confirms Ana's KYC level allows this amount, checks daily limits, and scores fraud risk (new device, unusual recipient). High risk may require step-up verification.

walkthrough.title: Start the transfer
walkthrough.text: The transfer orchestrator records the transfer as PENDING with the idempotency key.

walkthrough.title: Move balances atomically
walkthrough.text: In one database transaction the ledger debits Ana's wallet account and credits Sam's, with double-entry lines and a balance check. No bank is involved, so it is instant.

walkthrough.title: Notify the recipient
walkthrough.text: Sam gets a push notification that $20 arrived. Their balance is usable immediately.

walkthrough.title: Show the result
walkthrough.text: Ana's app shows COMPLETED and her new balance, read from the ledger.

walkthrough.title: Cash out to a bank
walkthrough.text: When Sam withdraws, the money leaves over ACH (1-3 days), real-time payments, or a push-to-card. The ledger shows it as pending until the rail confirms, and returns are reversed.

data.label: Wallet App
responsibilities: Authenticates the user strongly (biometrics, device binding).
Sends transfers with idempotency keys.
Shows clear pending vs completed states.

failureModes.impact: Money sent to a stranger; hard to recover.
failureModes.mitigation: Show the recipient's name and photo, and confirm on first send.
Device binding, step-up auth for new payees, velocity limits.

data.label: Wallet API
responsibilities: Authenticates and rate-limits every call.
Deduplicates by idempotency key.
Runs risk and limit checks before money moves.

failureModes.mitigation: Store idempotency key with the result; return it on retries.
Strict timeout; allow small low-risk transfers, hold large ones.

data.label: KYC, Limits & Fraud
responsibilities: Verifies identity at onboarding and raises limits with more verification.
Screens against sanctions lists (AML compliance).
Scores each transfer for fraud and money-mule patterns.

failureModes.impact: Authorised push payment fraud; reimbursement may be required.
failureModes.mitigation: Warnings for risky payees, delays for first large transfers, mule detection.
Graduated responses (step-up rather than block) and fast review.

data.label: Wallet Ledger
responsibilities: Holds every user's balance as ledger accounts.
Applies transfers atomically with no negative balances.
Tracks pending funds from bank rails separately.

failureModes.mitigation: Row locks or conditional updates on balance.
Daily reconciliation of the pooled bank account against total wallet balances.

data.label: Transfer Orchestrator
responsibilities: Drives each transfer through its states: PENDING → COMPLETED or FAILED.
Publishes events reliably through a transactional outbox.
Handles payouts that take days and may be returned.

failureModes.scenario: Ledger posted but event not published
failureModes.mitigation: Outbox written in the same transaction as the posting.

failureModes.impact: Money already spent from the wallet.
failureModes.mitigation: Hold periods for new users; negative balance recovery.

data.label: Bank Rails

input.name: Payout / top-up
input.type: Move $X to or from a linked account

responsibilities: Move real money in and out of the wallet's pooled bank account.
Settle in seconds (RTP) or days (ACH).
Report returns and failures.

failureModes.scenario: Top-up via ACH bounces after funds were spent
failureModes.mitigation: Treat ACH top-ups as pending; limit spending until they clear.
Queue and retry; offer alternative rails.

data.label: Recipient Notifications
responsibilities: Tells the recipient that money arrived.
Updates both users' activity feeds.
Respects privacy settings for public feeds.

failureModes.impact: Recipient sees the old balance and is confused.
failureModes.mitigation: Notify only after the ledger commit (outbox).
Private by default; clear visibility controls.
